#5601 fix(dependency_utils): preserve MSVC mutex compatibility in local dependency builds Past contributor Reviewed 2026-10-24 05:38Z No reply from the submitter or their bot. I'm going to close this. I would like to think that I'd do this on principle even if I was 100% sure the patch was correct, just like I wouldn't merge a patch from somebody who refused to sign a CLA. Whether the characters comprising the patch were generated by an LLM or somebody's squishy head-insides is really not the point, it's whether there's actually a person standing behind it who has seen it, understands it, and agrees that it's the best solution we can think of for the problem it tries to address. I feel like that is utterly lacking here. I trust that if the issue it's addressing is important, we'll eventually see different PR with a solution, coming from somebody who actually has the expertise and judgment to get it right.

We are going to merge that one with one extra guard for the root case, so I'll close this as a duplicate. One thing worth knowing from your diff: `{input: "/", want: "//"}` in the new table asserts a bug. ModSecurity's `normalize_path_inplace` returns `/` for `/`, `//` and `/a/../`; Coraza's wrapper re-appends `/` to the cleaned root. That is being fixed in #1742. If you want to keep contributing here, the three extra `normalisePathWin` rows you added (`\\server\share\file`, `C:foo/..`, `C:/foo:bar/baz`) are correct and would be welcome as a small follow-up to the corpus, and a Windows CI job for `./internal/transformations/...` (see #1140) is still open.

#4298 Speed up BinaryClassificationEvaluator threshold search ~10x with NumPy, using 3x less memory Past contributor 2026-11-05 12:37Z Hello! Thank you for the benchmarks and tests. I'm going to close this PR because the demonstrated benefit doesn't outweigh the readability cost. The NumPy version is a little shorter, but following grouped indices across several arrays and helper calls makes the threshold search harder to understand than the existing loops. The speedup is real. In my comparison, computing both thresholds for 1,000 pairs dropped from about 1.34 ms to 0.08 ms. That's the validation size used in our Quora examples, so the saving is about 1 ms per similarity function. The larger benchmarks show bigger savings, but don't establish how much this improves a full evaluation including model inference. I'd like performance improvements to keep the implementation simple and demonstrate a meaningful benefit in an actual evaluation workflow. I don't think this tradeoff is fully worthwhile based on the evidence here, but I'm interested in a smaller version for sure. - Tom Aarsen

Thanks for your PR, but we're going to decline listing this at this time. The community apps page exists to cover ground we don’t — desktop, terminal, web dashboards, integrations and monitoring tooling, where there’s no official Meshtastic client to use. Android and iOS aren’t in that category; we ship official apps on both, and those are what we point users to. So an alternative mobile client isn’t something we list. That’s a scope call about the page, not a judgment on your work. Separately, and regardless of the above: our trademark guidelines don’t permit the Meshtastic mark in third-party project names, including as a modifier — see the naming section of https://meshtastic.org/docs/legal/licensing-and-trademark/. `meshtastic-plus` falls under that, and we’d ask you to rename the repository. Your own branding, Mesh+ and meshplus.app, doesn’t raise the same issue, so this is only about the repo name.

#2599 Record which radio each row came through, and key messages by sender First-time contributor Reviewed 2026-10-31 16:08Z Thanks for splitting this out of #2588. Same answer as on #2600, though: connecting several radios at once isn't on our plan, and this changes the database for it before we've agreed on the design. Most of what it writes (observations, reception rows, `receivedBy`, the new `MyInfoEntity` fields) has nothing reading it yet, and every packet pays for it on the same write path we've been working to keep light. Once a schema change ships we carry it forever, so I don't want to take it ahead of the decision. If you'd like multi-radio, please start an issue or discussion with the design, and we can settle whether and how before any of the code lands. Some of this would be welcome on its own, as separate small PRs against `main`: - Messages from two nodes that share a packet id. That's a real bug. A PR with just the per-sender key and the duplicate check, plus the migration test, would be good to review. - The note when a channel switches preset, region or key. That's a new feature and could go in on its own if you want to pursue it. - Reading LoRa and channel settings as saved. If you can reproduce the stale preset on `main`, please open an issue with the steps first. Please also leave `research/` and `specs/` out of PRs. Those files don't belong in the repo.
#2600 Tag every radio event with the connection it came from First-time contributor Reviewed 2026-10-31 16:07Z Thanks for this. Connecting several radios at once isn't something we have planned, and with one radio this doesn't change what the app does, so I don't want to take groundwork for it into the receive path yet. That path handles every packet, and the second half of this change doesn't exist yet. If multi-radio is something you'd like to see, please open an issue or discussion with the design first: how the UI would show more than one radio, and how per-radio state (connect steps, heartbeats, the node DB) would be kept apart. Then we can decide on it before any of the code lands. On the stale-event fix: `main` already cancels the old connection's event task on disconnect, and `didReceive` drops data while closing or when there's no active connection. That leaves only a very short window, for an event already read from the old stream that gets handled after the new connection is set. If you've seen that cause a real problem, a small PR with just that fix and a way to reproduce it would be welcome.
#2588 Feature: Multi-radio support. First-time contributor 2026-10-31 16:07Z Thanks for the work here. Connecting several radios at once isn't on our plan, and at this size we can't review or merge it as one change. I've commented on #2599 and #2600, which split pieces out of this one. If you'd like the app to support multi-radio, please start with an issue or discussion covering the design: how the screens would show more than one radio, how each radio's data is kept apart, and what it costs on the packet path. Then we can decide whether and how before any code. The standalone fixes mentioned on #2599 are welcome as their own small PRs against `main`.
#2680 Make messaging a node easier from the Nodes tab First-time contributor Reviewed 2026-10-25 15:31Z Thanks for working on this, @dzienisz. We're going to close it. Swiping right on a row is the gesture Messages and Mail use to mark something read or unread. Putting Message on that swipe in the node list would confuse people who expect that behavior. The order of the node list's long-press menu was set across platforms in #1841, following the [menu alignment audit](https://github.com/meshtastic/design/blob/master/standards/audits/menu-alignment-audit.md#3-node-list--long-press-context-menu) in the design repo. Message is third there, after favorites and mute. If you think messaging should be higher, that's the place to raise it: open an issue in [meshtastic/design](https://github.com/meshtastic/design/issues) proposing the new order, so it changes on every client together.

#6355 TRUNK-6664: Implement deterministic bootstrap password mechanism First-time contributor Reviewed 2026-10-27 19:00Z @praisekavuma4 Thanks for your work on this; however, the design proposed in the underlying ticket is not something we should implement at all. Providing a pathway to reset a user's password to a deterministic value undermines the security of the system and is not something we should support. Instead, (and the ticket is not clear on _why_ we were pursuing this), we need to _carefully_ think about the goal we are trying to accomplish (examples): * Don't hard-code the admin password: this is somewhat handled by the installer, but we likely could do better. * Provide a way to create a user without specifying a password: the solution, then is to securely generate a _random_ password and make that available only once. * Resetting admin accounts: that is outside of the scope of OpenMRS core but seems to imply some other tool to work on it? Adding a mechanism to reset admin passwords inside the application (other than what already exists) trivially becomes a privilege escalation issue. This is the point where we need to clarify the use-case that we're trying to support.

#3863 Add LLM Papers First-time contributor Approved 2026-09-27 12:41Z ## Linked list issues ### This is a newsletter/magazine, not an awesome list The README is structured as a blog with rotating "Today's Pick", "This Week's Essential Reads (January 1-7, 2026)", trend dashboards, and subjective impact scores. This is fundamentally different from the standard awesome list format (`- [Name](url) - Description.`). Time-sensitive sections like "Today's Pick" and weekly reads become stale immediately and require constant maintenance. ### Top description uses prohibited patterns > A curated list of seminal and breakthrough papers in Large Language Models. "A curated list of..." is the explicitly prohibited pattern. > Read what matters. Skip the noise. 🎯 Tagline/CTA. Replace with a succinct description of what the subject is (Large Language Models). ### TOC includes "Contributing" The Contents section lists `🤝 Contributing`. The guidelines say the TOC "Must not feature Contributing or Footnotes sections." ### License badge in README ``` [![License: CC0-1.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-CC0_1.0-lightgrey.svg)] ``` The guidelines say: "Do not add the license name, text, or a Licence section to the readme." ### CTA buttons in Contributing section ``` Submit Paper - Click Here (badge button) ✅ Reviewed within 24 hours | 🏆 Contributors get credit | 💬 Join discussions ``` Marketing copy. The Contributing section should just link to contributing.md. ### Subjective "Impact Scores" ``` + Performance: █████████░ 94% + Innovation: ██████████ 96% + Practicality:█████████░ 90% ``` These are subjective ratings presented as data. Awesome lists should provide objective descriptions, not editorial scores. ### "Research Trends Dashboard" with speculative data The Mermaid chart and statistics ("Agentic AI (+520%)", "Vanilla RAG (-45%)") are speculative/editorial content, not curated resources. "Next Wave" predictions do not belong in an awesome list. ### Most content is in sub-pages The main README links to `categories/*.md` files for the actual 145 papers. The main README itself is a magazine-style landing page, not a curated list with entries. --- ## Minor issues - Emoji in every section heading adds visual noise. - "Last updated: January 9, 2026, 7:00 PM IST" is a manual timestamp that is already stale. - PR body description: "A curated list of seminal and breakthrough papers" uses the "A curated list of..." anti-pattern.

#5522 docs: document dropping socket middleware packets First-time contributor 2026-10-09 08:21Z For future readers: When a socket middleware neither calls `next()` nor `next(err)`, the packet is indeed ignored. In that case, the event handler is not called, no error is emitted, and acknowledgements are not sent. I added a note about this behavior in the Socket middlewares section of the server-side Socket instance documentation: https://socket.io/docs/v4/server-socket-instance/#socket-middlewares I also added a small warning that, while this can be useful for intentionally dropping packets, authorization failures are often better handled explicitly with `next(new Error(...))` or with an acknowledgement response from the event handler, so the client is not left waiting indefinitely.

Tips for your workflow

Run govulncheck regularly on your Go modules to catch known vulnerabilities in dependencies.

Enable npm audit in CI to catch vulnerabilities before they ship. Consider using --audit-level=high.

Use pip-audit or safety to scan your Python dependencies for known CVEs.

Run cargo audit in CI to catch known Rust dependency vulnerabilities.

Enable GitHub's secret scanning and push protection on all repositories to prevent credential leaks.
